data.gender_notes: Jamrah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Jamrah refers to rocky outcrops or protrusions, often associated with the stone pillars in the Grand Mosque in Mecca. The name Jamrah carries the meaning “Rocky outcrops” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jamrah usually hope their child will grow to embody rocky outcrops and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Jamrah is a place of spiritual significance, symbolizing a connection to the divine.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jamrah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: جمرة
in_arabic.meaning: الجميرة هي جزء من الحج حيث يرمي الحاج الجمرات
in_arabic.long_meaning: الجميرة في اللغة العربية تعني القطعة الصغيرة من الحصى أو الحجارة، وفي سياق الحج، تشير إلى الجمرات التي يرميها الحاج في منى خلال أيام التشريق. يأتي أصل الكلمة من 'جمر' الذي يعني الحصى أو الحجارة الصغيرة، ويرتبط بالطقوس الدينية للحج.

in_urdu.name: جمرہ
in_urdu.meaning: جمرہ حج کے دنوں میں جمرات رمانے کی رسم
in_urdu.long_meaning: اردو میں جمرہ کا مطلب ہے وہ پتھر یا کঙ্কر جو حج کے دوران منیٰ میں جمرات کو رمانے کی رسم میں استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ یہ لفظ عربی جذر 'جمر' سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے چھوٹے پتھر یا کঙ্কر، اور حج کی رسومات کے ساتھ منسلک ہے۔

in_hindi.name: जम्रह
in_hindi.meaning: हज के दौरान जेमरात फेंकने की रस्म
in_hindi.long_meaning: जम्रह का अर्थ है हज के दिनों में मिना में जेमरात को फेंकने की रस्म। यह शब्द 'जमर' से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है छोटे पत्थर या कंकड़, और यह हज की धार्मिक रस्मों से जुड़ा हुआ है।

in_pashto.name: جمره
in_pashto.meaning: د حج پرونو په منى كې د جمراتو اچول
in_pashto.long_meaning: پښتو کې جمره د حج د رسم په توګه منى کې د جمراتو اچول دي. دا کلمه د 'جمر' څخه اخیستل شوې ده، چې معنی یې کوچني ډبرې یا کنکر دي، او د حج د مذهبي رسم سره تړاو لري.

in_english.name: Jamrah
in_english.meaning: Ritual of stoning the devil during Hajj
in_english.long_meaning: Jamrah refers to the ritual of stoning the devil, a crucial part of the Hajj pilgrimage. It originates from the Arabic root 'j-m-r', meaning to gather or collect small stones or pebbles. During Hajj, pilgrims throw these stones at three pillars representing the devil in Mina, Saudi Arabia. This act symbolizes the rejection of evil and commemorates the story of Ibrahim (Abraham) who resisted Satan's temptations.

data.cultural_impact: Jamrah is a significant location in Islamic pilgrimage, known as the Hajj, where pilgrims perform the symbolic casting of pebbles at the pillars of Muzdalifah during the last day of the pilgrimage. This action is a symbol of expressing regret and seeking Allah’s forgiveness for past sins. After sunrise, pilgrims return to Mina and throw pebbles at the large pillars, representing the stoning of Satan.
data.spiritual_significance: The act of throw stones at the jamrah signifies the struggle to purify the heart, body, and soul from sins and impurities. The spiritual meaning behind this act is the belief in striving to live a life of righteousness and seeking God's eternal mercy, compassion, and forgiveness. This spiritual practice serves as an ongoing reminder to stay mindful of one's sins and to redouble efforts to avoid them, leading to a more conscious and faith-driven life.
